system.summary: Numbered code of 1,592 elements, the table Weber prints as WE025 (Weber 1979; page numbers not checked here): common words as single groups, longer words spelled from syllable groups, in no alphabetical order; a circle or diamond over a group adds -s.
system.sibling_key: Poinsett to Monroe, Buenos Aires 14 June 1814 (catalogue 651; M37 roll 2 frame 0098, Duplicate 0100), same code with a clerk's interlinear decode, printed by Manning 1925 vol. 1 doc. 201.
system.notes: Identified as WE025 on 11 Nov 2026 by Andrew Beling (beling/README.md). That the table is Weber's could not be checked from the repository (341 of 1,592 rows are in it, 10 marked as checked on the page image); the numbering is confirmed apart from Weber by the clerk's 1814 decipherment, Dudout's 1811 values and the 1813 text. 1315, written where 'a' is wanted three times in the 1814 letter, is 'hu' in the table (not explained); 1215 = a. Cross and caret read from use only: the cross doubles a letter, the caret adds -ed. distinct_symbols 256 is the count of the first transcription (ciphertext_1813.txt); the second transcription has 245 distinct numbers.

prior_solution.where: 1813: Manning 1925 vol. 2 doc. 442 prints the cipher places as '(undeciphered cipher)'; no decipherment found. 1814 (catalogue 651): the clerk's interlinear decode on the RC, printed in Manning 1925 vol. 1 doc. 201 (found 27 Oct 2026). The code table: Weber 1979 prints WE025 in full; no reading of the 1813 letter with it found (the contributor's search of Weber, this repository, Tomokiyo's Cryptiana and Manning, 11 Nov 2026; not repeated at integration).

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue 639 task page. The WE025 identification and the 1813 reading were contributed by Andrew Beling, with AI agents (pull request 414); the project verified and integrated them.

solution.what: Manning vol. 2 doc. 442 read for the clear context; web search for a decipherment or the 1810 cypher: none found.
Fetched M37 roll 2 frames 0091-0102 from the NARA catalogue; the letter is at 0092-0094.
Transcribed passages P1-P9 (437 groups, 256 distinct) line by line; P0 on frame 0092 illegible after background flattening.
Applied the repo's US code tables (JQA/Department 1803-40, Armstrong THE=972, Pinckney, 1788 legation, Jefferson 1787, Mountflorence 1801) directly: noise.
shift_test.py: every constant shift and mod 1600/1700 of the same tables, scored with lang en-modern 4-gram; best z 4.3 among about 9,000 settings, junk decodes.
Sumter, Rio 1813 (M121 vol. 1A frames 0035-0039, interlinear decode) checked: the = 798, of = 1399; a different code.
Poinsett 14 June 1814 (frame 0098, duplicate 0100) found in the same code with a clerk's interlinear decode; 88 values aligned into key_1814.tsv.
decode.py applied the sibling key to the 1813 groups: 158 of 437 have a value; fragments, no sentence reads yet.

Context pass over the 1813 decode: only 'Lima' (249 413, twice in the Lima paragraph) cross-checks sibling syllables; no new values, the other unknown groups occur once or twice in contexts that do not fix them.
Weber 1979 not online; the HSP calendar of the Poinsett papers (1941, HathiTrust full view) is behind a bot check and was not searched.
Lowry, La Guaira 1810-12, held a cypher for the 1810 agents (Manning); M84 roll 1 frames 0014-0090 viewed: no code; M37 roll 1 (Shaler) has no code frames.
Catalogue 651, 14 June 1814: RC (0097-0098) and Duplicate (0099-0100) transcribed line by line with the clerk's glosses; merged text 123 groups, 90 distinct (ciphertext_1814.txt).
Manning vol. 1 (1925) doc. 201, pp. 335-336 prints the 14 June 1814 letter with both code passages in clear: the clerk's decode word for word. Catalogue 651 was already deciphered.

Clerk's decode checked group by group against both copies and Manning: 122 of 123 groups carry a value; key corrections 964 principle, 1236 it, 1087 two, 737 between, 1179 ct / 765 ion, 480 t; group 39 unglossed.
decode.py re-run on the 1813 letter with the corrected key: 161 of 437 groups have a value (was 158); still fragments.
Manning vols. 1-2 searched for other Poinsett letters with code: none decoded besides 14 June 1814.

Beling contribution: the numerals of P1-P9 transcribed afresh from frames 0093-0094 and frozen (sha256 d31b3043...) before WE025 was tried; doubtful digits kept open as {a|b}; not blind (the repo decode had been seen). Against transcription.tsv: 425 of 437 groups agree (420 first readings, 5 second), 5 differ, 7 have an unread digit in one or both (beling/transcription/, beling/decryption_1813-02-20.txt).

Beling contribution: code 1355 identified as WE025, printed in full by Weber 1979, pp. 470-480 (1,592 elements). Table transcribed from the book's text layer, 16 places checked on the page images, frozen by sha256 at 2026-11-11T10:37:23Z before any decoding; one correction after the freeze (668 fect). Against key_1814.tsv, 27 values differ: 21 syllable splits, 462/1495 dra-w with 39 = should, 618 iu, 337/435 transcription errors (338 never, 485 dom), 1315 = hu not explained.

Beling contribution: 14 June 1814 decoded with WE025 alone and compared with the clerk's decipherment: 0.935 of letters matched (376 of 401); 200 shuffled keys mean 0.184, best 0.306, z 16.3; 0.954 with the two image rereads. Not blind: the agent had seen the clerk's values; no threshold declared (beling/tests/heldout_1814_result.txt).

Beling contribution: 20 Feb 1813 decoded with WE025 from the frozen numerals: 406 of 437 groups read as frozen (92.9%), 4 after an image reread, 20 on an assumed digit misread (not confirmed), 7 holes; all nine passages P1-P9 join Manning's clear text; P0 still illegible. Read in part, read_share 0.916 (beling/reading_1813-02-20.md).

Beling contribution: prior art for a tie between Poinsett's code and WE025 searched in Weber 1979, this repository (files, open and closed pull requests and issues, commits of 9-11 Nov 2026), Tomokiyo's Cryptiana and Manning 1925. Nothing found.

Integration of pull request 414 after a separate read-only verification: hashes, status counts (D 385, A 21, R 4, I 20, H 7) and the 1814 score (0.935, 376 of 401 letters; 0.954 with two rereads) reproduce; a decoder written separately, applied to the first transcription (transcription.tsv), gives 432 of 437 groups a value and the same English; 73 of 73 groups on frame 0093 agree with the frozen numerals; 485 and 1315 (three times) confirmed on frame 0100. Not reproducible from the repository: the 200-shuffle control (full table absent; a shuffle of the committed rows gives mean 0.194, best 0.307) and the identity of the table with Weber's print (book absent; page numbers 470-480 against 443-453 unresolved). The 1814 test is not blind and had no threshold. Read share restated by the read bar: 248 of 294 coded word places (0.844; 264 with the 16 choice words; contributor's 0.916 includes Manning's clear words); groups 385 of 437 as first frozen (0.881; 406 with the choices). outcome.key recovered -> partial; contribution 'key extended or corrected' removed. One pass over eleven of the twenty assumed misreads on frame 0093: none settled on the high-contrast film (P7.4 reads ?517, which supports 1517).

The contributor's follow-up commit c0538294 to pull request 414 (after the integration above): his own reading review of the 1813 reading (grade A), and the reading file now marks two supplied words ([the] in [?to] [the]; marke[12] for the word that had a hole) and two reread groups ([?the] in on [?the] part, [?seas]) that the project's write-up already marked. Checked against the file and the page: no figure of the groups moves; the supplied [the] is counted like [be], so the strict count is 248 of 294 word places (0.844; was 248 of 293, 0.846).

outcome.notes: 1813: read in part with the printed table WE025, contributed by Andrew Beling with AI agents (beling/README.md), verified and integrated 12 Nov 2026 (NOTES, Integration check). A printed key was matched; nothing was recovered by cryptanalysis, and outcome.key is partial because seven groups have no usable value. codes_open: five numbers (55, 502, 487, 122, 1261) occur once each and give no sense; 12 and 774 give sense elsewhere but not at one place each (7 tokens), among the 245 distinct numbers of the second transcription (the first has 256). The 1814 letter (651) is complete from the existing decipherment; with WE025 its group 39 is 'should'; 1315 (three times, where 'a' is wanted) is not explained.

texts.label: Poinsett to Monroe, Santiago, 20 Feb 1813, M37 roll 2 frames 0092-0094 (catalogue 639), with the table WE025
texts.summary: Writing from Santiago while the Carreras governed Chile and Lima's cruisers blockaded Valparaiso and Conception (Manning's clear text), Poinsett reports in code that he has taken a part in the revolution beyond his instructions, that a small naval force with five thousand stand of arms would insure the fall of Lima, that his journey to Arauco is really to leave the militia in patriot hands before independence is declared, and that the new governor of the bishopric, proposed by him, is at his disposal.
texts.note: Contributed by Andrew Beling with AI agents (beling/README.md). read_share is the strict count of the coded words only: 248 of 294 word places (292 words and the supplied be and the) whose every group is a first frozen reading used as the table gives it; choice, reread, assumed-misread, hole and supplied words are not counted (264 with the 16 choice words). The contributor's 0.916 also counts Manning's clear words. The reading file marks the reread and assumed-misread words [?word]; the 16 choice words are listed in NOTES (Integration check). The decryption is laid out against Daniel Bourdeau's transcription.tsv. P0 (frame 0092) not read.

reading_review.by: integration reader for the project, after the contributor's AI agents
reading_review.note: Read as English sentences against decryption_1813-02-20.txt and Manning's clear text on both sides of each passage: all nine passages construe and join the clear text; holes are marked and scattered, thickest in P7 (court of Brasil, B. Ayres), where four words rest on assumed misreads. Frame 0093 looked at for eleven doubtful groups; no human has read the reading. The contributor recorded his own review of the same file on 12 Nov 2026 (grade A, with two independent AI-agent readings): P1-P9 coherent, five unexplained groups and about twenty marked guesses scattered, P0 unread; on that review he marked two supplied words and two reread groups in the reading.

texts.label: Poinsett to Monroe, Buenos Aires, 14 June 1814, M37 roll 2 frames 0097-0100 (catalogue 651), from the clerk's decipherment
texts.summary: From Buenos Aires Poinsett reports in code that the government there will seek British protection at any price if Britain and Spain break, though the people will never let the English gain a permanent footing; and that British trade is exposed to retaliation with seldom more than a single frigate to protect it, two sloops of war being better than a frigate in waters where a ship should draw eighteen feet at most.
texts.note: The words are the State Department clerk's of 1814, printed by Manning 1925 (vol. 1 doc. 201). read_share: 83 of 86 coded word places; the three places where Poinsett wrote 1315 and the sense wants 'a' are not counted (the clerk wrote nothing there; WE025 has 'hu').

reading_review.note: Both passages read as English sentences against the clerk's words (reading_1814.txt) and the WE025 line-by-line decode (beling/tests/heldout_1814_result.txt); they join the clear text Manning prints.
